title: Fault tolerance of quantum circuits with tensor networks and symplectic geometry
authors: Soham Ghosh, Holger Boche, Andrew Tanggara
abstract: We develop an operator-algebraic framework for analyzing fault tolerance in quantum circuits and establish necessary and sufficient conditions for fault tolerance under any given noise model. For prescribed circuit families and noise models, we derive a semidefinite program (SDP) based test whose infeasibility certifies that there does not exist any recovery map restoring its intended operation. For non-adaptive stabilizer circuits, analyzing the stabilizer symmetries of its components with symplectic geometry, we obtain closed-form detection and logical-effect matrices that characterize circuit distance algebraically. Applied to a finite Hastings--Haah honeycomb Floquet-code circuit, these matrices certify the dynamical encoding of two logical qubits and distance four under Pauli noise including measurement errors. Using these matrices, we then derive MacWilliams identities for circuit weight enumerators and obtain linear-programming (LP) upper bounds on circuit distance. Output-code constraints give additional Singleton-like bounds. Under independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) depolarizing noise, the weight enumerators determine decoder failure probabilities and yield upper bounds on finite-circuit pseudothresholds. Finally, we derive LP distance bounds for families of flag syndrome-extraction circuits specified by their CNOT orderings, by incorporating the $t$-flag criterion as additional linear constraints to the distance-bounding LP. An analytical CSS Hamming-code benchmark yields a tight distance-three bound attained by the Chao--Reichardt one-flag construction.
summary: This paper presents an advanced, mathematically rigorous framework for determining the fault tolerance of quantum circuits. It uses tools from symplectic geometry and linear programming to derive necessary and sufficient conditions and upper bounds on circuit distance. This work is crucial for designing reliable quantum computation protocols by quantifying resilience against noise.
main_problem: The paper develops a rigorous framework to analyze the fault tolerance of quantum circuits under various noise models to ensure reliable quantum computation.
main_result: It establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for fault tolerance and derives linear-programming (LP) bounds on circuit distance using algebraic tools like weight enumerators and symplectic geometry.
method: The methodology combines operator-algebraic frameworks, semidefinite programming (SDP) tests, and the use of symplectic geometry to characterize stabilizer symmetries.
model_or_system: The focus is on abstract quantum circuits, specifically non-adaptive stabilizer circuits, analyzed using circuit-noise models and quantum error-correcting codes.
key_observables: Circuit distance ($d_{	ext{circ}, \zeta}$), detection syndrome, logical-effect matrices, and failure probabilities.
important_parameters: Noise models (e.g., depolarizing noise, Pauli noise), circuit structure (e.g., Hastings--Haah honeycomb Floquet-code), and the level of abstraction ($\zeta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes specific noise characteristics (e.g., i.i.d. depolarizing noise) or relies on the feasibility of LP relaxations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates an adaptive circuit interacting with temporally correlated noise, detailing components like quantum instruments and noise maps.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing general recovery conditions via SDP tests to specializing the analysis using symplectic geometry for non-adaptive stabilizer circuits, culminating in the derivation of weight enumerators and LP distance bounds.
why_interesting: The deep mathematical machinery connecting symplectic geometry, algebraic coding theory (MacWilliams identities), and fault tolerance provides powerful, general tools for assessing the robustness of quantum computation protocols.
